title: Miniature Plumbing Pipe Routing 3D Editor Diorama
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a miniature plumbing pipe routing 3D editor diorama. The scene represents a cutaway cross-section of a small building where the user can place, connect, and route plumbing pipes in 3D.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (8, 10, 8) looking at origin. Enable OrbitControls for rotation/zoom but with constrained polar angle (10-80 degrees) and distance (5-20).
- Add a directional light at (5, 12, 5) intensity 1.2, ambient light intensity 0.4, and a subtle hemisphere light (sky: 0x87CEEB, ground: 0x8B7355, intensity 0.3).
- Create a diorama base: a 10x0.3x10 box (wood-colored 0xDEB887) representing a floor slab. Add thin translucent walls (0xCCCCCC, opacity 0.15) on two sides to suggest a cutaway building.
- Render a 10x10 grid of snap points on the floor (1 unit spacing), visualized as small cyan dots (radius 0.05). These are the valid placement nodes.
- The grid uses integer coordinates from (-4,-4) to (5,5) mapped to world XZ positions.

## Pipe System
- Pipes are cylindrical segments (radius 0.08, color 0x708090 metallic) connecting two adjacent grid nodes (horizontally, vertically on XZ, or vertically in Y up to 3 levels: Y=0.3, Y=1.3, Y=2.3).
- Support 3 pipe types selectable via keyboard: [1] = Cold Water (blue 0x4488FF), [2] = Hot Water (red 0xFF4444), [3] = Drain (gray 0x666666, radius 0.12 larger).
- Pipe segments snap between adjacent grid nodes (Manhattan neighbors including vertical). Each segment stores: startNode, endNode, pipeType, segmentId.
- Elbow joints (small sphere radius 0.12, matching pipe color) auto-appear at nodes where exactly 2 pipes meet at an angle. T-joints (slightly larger sphere 0.15) appear where 3 pipes meet.

## Placement Interaction
- Click a grid node to select it as pipe start (highlight it yellow). Click a second adjacent node to place a pipe segment between them. If nodes are not adjacent, show a brief red flash on the second node and reject.
- Right-click a pipe segment to delete it. Deleting updates joints automatically.
- Press [U] to undo last action (place or delete), [R] to redo. Maintain an undo stack of up to 50 actions.

## Fixtures
- Press [F] to enter fixture placement mode. In this mode, clicking a node with at least one pipe connection places a fixture. Cycle fixture types with [Tab]: Faucet, Toilet, Showerhead. Fixtures are represented by distinct colored boxes (Faucet: 0xC0C0C0 small 0.2 cube, Toilet: 0xFFFFF0 0.3x0.25x0.35 box, Showerhead: 0xE8E8E8 0.15x0.4x0.15 tall box). Press [F] again to exit fixture mode.
- Each fixture must connect to at least one cold water pipe. Toilets and Showerheads also require a drain pipe on the same node. Validate on placement; reject with red flash if requirements not met.

## Water Flow Simulation
- Press [Space] to toggle water flow simulation. When active, animate small blue spheres (radius 0.03) traveling along cold water pipes, red spheres along hot water pipes, and gray spheres along drain pipes at speed 2 units/sec.
- Flow particles spawn at source nodes (nodes at grid edge with exactly one pipe connection) and travel toward fixtures. Maintain exactly 3 particles per active pipe segment during simulation.
- Display flow rate in a HUD: total active pipe segments, total flow particles, simulation time in seconds.

## Validation System
- Press [V] to run a validation check. The system verifies: (a) all fixtures have required pipe connections, (b) no orphan pipe segments (every segment is reachable from a source node), (c) no pipe type conflicts (cold and hot cannot share the same segment). Display results in a DOM panel: green checkmark or red X for each rule, plus total pipe length (sum of segment lengths in units).

## Level System
- Press [L] to cycle active building level: 0, 1, 2. Pipes on inactive levels become semi-transparent (opacity 0.2). The active level is highlighted. Vertical pipes connecting levels always remain visible.

## HUD / DOM Elements
- Top-left: current pipe type name and color swatch, fixture mode indicator, active level number.
- Top-right: pipe count, fixture count, total pipe length (formatted to 2 decimals), joint count.
- Bottom-center: validation results panel (hidden until [V] pressed).
- All DOM elements should have descriptive id attributes.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- pipeSegments: array of {id, startNode:{x,y,z}, endNode:{x,y,z}, pipeType:string, length:number}
- fixtures: array of {id, node:{x,y,z}, fixtureType:string, valid:boolean}
- joints: array of {node:{x,y,z}, connectionCount:number, jointType:string}
- selectedPipeType: string ('cold'|'hot'|'drain')
- activeLevel: number (0|1|2)
- fixtureMode: boolean
- flowSimActive: boolean
- flowParticleCount: number
- simTime: number
- totalPipeLength: number
- totalPipeCount: number
- totalFixtureCount: number
- totalJointCount: number
- undoStackSize: number
- redoStackSize: number
- validationResult: {allFixturesValid:boolean, noOrphans:boolean, noConflicts:boolean, totalLength:number} or null
- lastAction: string ('place_pipe'|'delete_pipe'|'place_fixture'|'undo'|'redo'|'none')
- cameraDistance: number
- selectedNode: {x,y,z} or null
physics_constraints: Pipes must snap to integer grid nodes only. Pipe segments connect Manhattan-adjacent nodes (distance exactly 1.0 in one axis). Total pipe length must equal the sum of individual segment lengths (conservation). Flow particles must travel at constant 2 units/sec. Vertical pipes only at Y levels 0.3, 1.3, 2.3. No two pipe segments may overlap (same start and end nodes). Joint types must be consistent with connection count (2=elbow, 3=T-joint). Fixture validation rules must be strictly enforced.
